summary: Darwin Notify is a system-wide, name-keyed notification facility with integer tokens, state values and kernel-level delivery. BifrOSt has no equivalent: the nearest app-facing counterpart is the Foundation-style DistributedNotificationCenter, which relays string-named broadcasts between running apps through the shell. System event names (time zone, mounts, clock, network) are not broadcast to apps by name.

features.note: Cross-app broadcast relayed by the shell (ToShell::DistPost). The SDK sorts the user info, keeps at most 32 entries with values cut to 1024 characters, and gives the sender's own observers the same payload (distributed_user_info, tested in parity_sdk-complete-24). Headless tests: a_distributed_post_reaches_local_observers_and_is_queued_for_the_shell_sorted, a_process_local_distributed_post_sends_nothing_to_the_shell, notify_bus_calls_go_to_the_notify_bus_service_with_their_method. Only between BifrOSt apps with string names; no system-wide notification bus exists here, so posting across processes outside BifrOSt needs the lab machine. Verify on Midget for parity.

features.note: Observers run on the main thread, take an optional object filter, and can be suspended and resumed through their token (tested in parity_sdk-complete-24). Headless tests: an_observer_hears_its_name_and_its_object_only, an_observer_without_an_object_hears_every_object_and_gets_the_user_info. Gap: observer closures are tied to the main thread and there is no queue argument, since the runtime has no second queue to bind an observer to. Verify on Midget for parity.

features.note: Cancelling removes a token, suspending skips posts while resume restarts delivery, and is_valid answers for a live token. The in-process observer token now suspends and resumes too, and a suspended observer leaves the others on its name running (parity_sdk-complete-24). Headless tests: cancelled_tokens_stop_receiving_posts, suspended_tokens_miss_posts_and_resume_restarts_delivery, an_observer_hears_its_name_and_its_object_only (dropping the token removes the observer). Verify on Midget for parity.

features.apple: notify_post delivery when target not running
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 4 (theme-09, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. An app that is not running misses the post, equal to Apple's drop behaviour, with no option to hold it.

features.bifrost: springboard/core/src/notify_center.rs (SYSTEM_EVENTS, volume_change); springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01d.rs; springboard/core/tests/parity_sdk-complete-24.rs; wired: springboard/src/shell/services/notify_bus.rs (system.appearance.change, system.screen.locked, system.screen.unlocked, system.network.change, system.contacts.change, system.calendar.change, system.timezone.change, system.hostname.change, system.volume.mount, system.volume.unmount)
features.note: The eleven system names are constants in the core model under the system namespace. The shell posts appearance, screen lock, network, contacts, calendar, time zone, host name and volume mount or unmount changes, polling the time zone and host name files and the mount table once a second. Gap: clock set, low disk space, disk-cache and log database names have no source in the shell (they need a wall-clock jump monitor, a free-space probe and the cache and log stores), so they are not posted; the lab machine must confirm the file-based names. Verify on Midget for parity.
Return codes of the Darwin C API; not applicable to the BifrOSt SDK.

gaps: No system-wide named notifications from the kernel or system services (time zone, clock, mount, network, disk space) to apps.
No notify_check, notify_register_signal, notify_set_state or notify_get_state equivalents.
No suspend or resume of observers, and no hold-for-later delivery to apps that are not running.
Observers always run on the main thread; no caller-chosen dispatch queue.
Broadcast payloads are string to string with a 32-entry and 1024-character cap per value.
